verdict.rationale: First-party Entra docs say users can register and sign in passwordlessly with passkeys (FIDO2) on security keys, native or third-party passkey providers, or Microsoft Authenticator, which covers the core of the story. The community-reported FIDO downgrade attack depends on an alternative fallback method being enabled; it is a hardening caveat, not evidence that passwordless sign-in fails. missing for 10: explicit documentation of platform biometrics (e.g., Windows Hello) as a passwordless method, independent hands-on corroboration of the employee sign-in flow.

support.subject: As an employee, I can sign in without a password — passwordless flows via passkeys, authenticator, or platform biometrics documented and supported

citations.quote: passkeys (FIDO2) offer a frictionless sign-in experience by eliminating passwords, reducing prompts, and enabling fast, secure authentication across devices

users in your organization can then register and sign in to their Microsoft Entra account using a passkey stored on a FIDO2 security key, a native or third-party passkey provider, or in Microsoft Authenticator
